test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 25 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
In the address regarding the Union Budget 2024, the Finance Minister highlighted key areas of focus for the upcoming year. 

Which of the following sectors was emphasised?

options.text: Employment, Skilling, MSMEs and the Middle Class

solution:
The correct answer is __**Employment, Skilling, MSMEs and the Middle Class**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the** Union Budget 2024**, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman emphasized sectors including employment, skilling, Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and the middle class.
 
• This **focus aligns with the government's commitment to fostering economic growth and ensuring inclusive development.**
 
• The government **introduced three schemes under the Prime Minister's package to promote employment, focusing on EPFO enrollments, recognition of first-time employees, and support for both employees and employers**.
 
• Additionally, **a new centrally sponsored scheme aims to skill 20 lakh youth over five years, with 1,000 Industrial Training Institutes being upgraded in a hub-and-spoke model.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The major terms related to the Union Budget include the following:**
 
• **Revenue Budget:** Details the government's revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) and revenue expenditure. It focuses on the regular operating costs of the government.
 
• **Capital Budget: **Involves government expenditure on the acquisition of assets like land, buildings, machinery, and includes receipts from loans, investments, etc.
 
• **Fiscal Deficit: **The difference between the total expenditure and total revenue (excluding borrowings) of the government. It indicates the borrowing requirement for the government.
 
• **Revenue Deficit:** The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts. It highlights the shortfall in day-to-day government operations funding.
 
• **Primary Deficit:** The fiscal deficit minus interest payments on previous borrowings. It shows the borrowing requirement of the government, excluding debt interest payments.
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):** The total value of all goods and services produced within the country. It's used to gauge the health of the economy.
 
• **Direct Taxes**: Taxes directly levied on individuals and corporations, such as income tax and corporate tax.
 
• **Indirect Taxes:** Taxes levied on goods and services rather than on income or profits, like Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• **Non-Tax Revenue: **Government revenue from sources other than taxes, such as profits from public sector enterprises and fees from services.
 
• **Plan vs. Non-Plan Expenditure**: Plan expenditure refers to spending on the implementation of economic plans. Non-plan expenditure includes costs related to routine government operations and obligations.
